_note: One scene_beats record per scene, keyed by `scene` (stored as parent_id). `driver` is who wants in the scene and may differ from who acts first. A beat's `action.by` / `reaction.by` may be a character, a LOCATION or a WORLD — that is the demo's case of a place acting. `changes[].entity` may be a character, relationship, location or world; only where something changed. `gap` stops at the break, it does not resolve it. No `value_turns` here — those are the next layer, written once the beats exist.

reaction.subtext: refusing the question by answering it honestly about something else

sections.Notes: The demo's case of a scene where the driver and the actor of the first beat are the same person, and the scene ends on the OTHER character acting alone. Also the case of a `changes` entry on two characters where neither change is dramatic: both know slightly more and neither will act on it.

sections.Notes: The demo's case of a LOCATION acting: `the-cyclone` is the `by` on every action side, because in this scene the place is the character and the person is the object. No `true_character` moment, because nobody makes a choice. The beats are all gap and no dialogue, which is what a transition looks like on the page.

sections.Notes: The demo's case of a `changes` entry on a character who never appears: the Witch of the East is dead, is in the cast, and is the object of a change in a scene she is not in. Also the first `changes` entry on a RELATIONSHIP, recording the withholding rather than the meeting.

sections.Notes: The demo's clearest case of the driver acting and reacting in the same beat: the fourth beat has the Scarecrow on both sides, because his own competence is what he is arguing with. It is also the case of a `gap` that opens and is closed by nobody — the audience sees the contradiction the character cannot.

sections.Notes: The demo's densest scene: four `changes` entries covering a character, a relationship, and a second relationship — and two `true_character` moments in one scene, which is the maximum the field is designed for. The `tin-man-queen-of-the-field-mice` change is recorded here even though she is not in the scene, because the debt begins when he becomes able to be owed.

sections.Notes: The demo's `non-event` beat sheet: no plot moves, there is no `true_character` choice, and the location is the actor throughout. It is the case for `changes` accepting a LOCATION as the entity that changed — the field is holding three people and Dorothy is alone, and neither fact is a plot beat. This record is deleted with its scene in Draft 3.

sections.Notes: The demo's Cameo character carrying the scene's `true_character` moment, which is the point of separating `driver` from the choice. Also the case of a `changes` entry on a relationship where the change is only that something was noticed.

sections.Notes: The demo's case of the DRIVER being the antagonist rather than the protagonist: the Wizard wants and the Wizard wins, and Dorothy is the one who changes. Four `changes` entries here, three of them on characters who each lose something different — and `the-wizard` never appears in the flesh, only as a voice and a shape in a chair.

sections.Notes: The demo's case of the antagonist as `driver` with no dialogue of her own in the scene — she never speaks, only sends. The `true_character` moment is the Lion's and the driver is the Witch, which is the widest separation between driver and choice in the demo. Also the case of a `changes` entry on the Wizard, who is nowhere near the scene.

sections.Notes: The demo's only scene with a two-character cast and no third party, which is why it can carry five beats without feeling crowded. The `true_character` moment belongs to the ANTAGONIST, and the `changes` entry on the relationship is the story admitting the grievance is real.

sections.Notes: The demo's case of a climax that is not a choice: Dorothy's `true_character` moment is absent because she saves a friend without deliberating, and the choice the scene records belongs to the Lion. Five `changes` entries, the densest in the demo, and one of them lands on a relationship that is not present — the field mice's debt, which the danger's ending has just made unpayable.

sections.Notes: The demo's case of the fraud being resolved by admission rather than punishment. The `changes` entry on `emerald-city` is a LOCATION changing state because of an event, which is the same mechanism as the `variant_of` transformation — this is the scene where the base and variant location differ as a consequence of what happens in it.

reaction.subtext: choosing the thing she belongs to over the place she belongs in

beats.gap: She is one step from home and the step is taken in the other direction.

action.surface: (shouting down) 'It'll come back! I'll come back!'
action.subtext: making a promise he has no way to keep, because it is the only comfort available

reaction.surface: 'He said a lot of things.'
reaction.subtext: declining to be comforted

beats.gap: The last thing the fraud does is lie kindly, and nobody is fooled and nobody minds.

sections.Notes: The demo's case of a character acting as the `reaction` with no dialogue and no intention: `toto` runs the wrong way and that is the turning point. The `changes` entry lands on the relationship rather than on Dorothy alone, because what changed is between the two of them and neither will ever mention it.

fields.scene_objective: to discharge three obligations with what is in the cupboard before the balloon
fields.turning_point: The Tin Man looks at the silk heart and begins to weep, and the weeping seizes his jaw

true_character.dilemma: admit the gifts are worthless and leave three people with nothing, or give them symbols and let the symbols do the work
true_character.choice_reveals: He chooses the symbols and defends them with complete sincerity, and they work — the gifts are chosen with real care by a man who has just called himself a fraud, which is the strongest evidence against his own account of himself

changes.change: holds a diploma and considers himself answered, without having changed at all
weeps over a silk heart, which proves to him that the gift is real
wears a medal, is still frightened, and has decided that both can be true
the argument has been settled in neither direction and both of them are satisfied

action.surface: 'I have decided to give you what I have.'
action.subtext: lowering the promise to something he can meet

reaction.surface: accepts a diploma
reaction.subtext: taking the first thing offered that answers the shape of the request

beats.gap: He asked for a brain and has been handed a piece of paper.

action.surface: 'Nobody who has one can be called a fool... that is the entire system and it has never once failed.'
action.subtext: defending certification with complete sincerity

reaction.surface: accepts the reasoning
reaction.subtext: relieved to have the question closed by an authority

beats.gap: The justification is a joke at the expense of institutions and it is entirely true, and it works.

action.surface: gives the Tin Man a silk heart and says wear it and see whether you weep
action.subtext: setting up a test he knows the man will pass

reaction.surface: weeps, which seizes his jaw, which makes him weep more
reaction.subtext: proving the gift by being unable to stop proving it

beats.gap: He asked for the capacity and has been given a demonstration of it that he supplied himself.

action.surface: 'Nothing makes anyone brave. It will remind you that somebody once thought you were.'
action.subtext: telling the truth about the medal instead of selling it

reaction.surface: puts it on and stands up straighter and is still frightened
reaction.subtext: accepting that both things are true at once

beats.gap: He has been given the honest answer, which is the only gift in the scene that is not a trick.

action.surface: 'I have nothing for you. I'm sorry. I'm going to get in a balloon.'
action.subtext: leaving before the one person he cannot satisfy can respond

reaction.surface: is not given a scene of her own to react in
reaction.subtext: being denied even the courtesy of a refusal

beats.gap: Three wishes are answered and the fourth is not, and the fourth is the one the story is about.

sections.Notes: The demo's case of a `true_character` moment for the fraud that is also his second-best action: he gives worthless things with real care. Four `changes` entries, three of them recording that nothing changed — which is the point, and the reason `changes` is only for what actually moved.

fields.scene_objective: to get home now that there is nobody left to ask
fields.turning_point: Glinda says it was all on the first day, and that she withheld it

true_character.dilemma: be angry that she could have gone home fourteen scenes ago, or accept the answer and use it
true_character.choice_reveals: She asks nothing about the delay and knocks her heels together — she takes the answer and leaves the grievance, which is the one active move she makes in the whole story

true_character.dilemma: defend the withholding as wisdom, or admit she enjoyed watching
true_character.choice_reveals: 'I did not tell you then because you would not have believed me and you would have stayed' — she offers the justification and does not close the question, which is why the story can leave her ambiguous

changes.change: is going home by her own act, having been given nothing she did not already have
is told he always had a brain, and has decided to believe it
is told he always had a heart, and has decided to believe it
is told he was brave throughout, and is not convinced, which is correct
has ended with the withholding named and not condemned

action.surface: 'I want to go home and there's nobody left to ask.'
action.subtext: reporting that every agent has been exhausted

reaction.surface: 'There never was. The shoes.'
reaction.subtext: answering a fourteen-scene problem in four words

beats.gap: She expects to be told there is no way and is told there always was.

action.surface: 'The shoes are powerful. You said that. They haven't done anything.'
action.subtext: holding the earlier promise to account

reaction.surface: 'They haven't been asked.'
reaction.subtext: making the failure of the object into the girl's oversight

beats.gap: The tool worked the whole time and nobody told her it needed using.

action.surface: 'It was all on the first day. I did not tell you then because you would not have believed me and you would have stayed.'
action.subtext: converting a withholding into a lesson after the fact

reaction.surface: does not argue about the delay and asks about Aunt Em
reaction.subtext: declining the grievance because the answer matters more

beats.gap: She is handed a justification and does not examine it, which is either grace or exhaustion.

action.surface: 'You won't come back. That's all right. Knowing the way is the same as being able to come.'
action.subtext: letting her go without asking her to promise

reaction.surface: knocks her heels together three times and says there is no place like home
reaction.subtext: using the answer and leaving

beats.gap: She wanted a place and has been told she already had one, and she goes without confirming it.

sections.Notes: The demo's only scene with TWO `true_character` moments, one for the protagonist and one for the mentor, and the two are opposites: Dorothy declines a grievance, Glinda declines to fully defend herself. Five `changes` entries, four on characters and one on a relationship, which is the densest closing scene the demo has.
